summary: Today's three approvals were sound on process. The open, though, was the sharp relief rally the Market Analyst had named as the main risk to his risk-off call. The spy_value series rose about 4.7% (539.98 to 565.41). The agent made +$3.63 (+0.6%) at 47.6% invested, while the shadow book at 99.4% invested made about +1.9%. The agent's lead over the shadow since version 6 narrowed, but it still holds: -1.71% against -2.83%, with SPY at -3.68%. One day of P&L does not grade these calls. Judged on reasoning: (1) The WMT sale (P1, filled $126.32) honoured a stored clause that was met: XLP 21d +0.52%, below +3%. The PM's point that rewriting a clause on the day it trips would make stored invalidations meaningless is the right rule. Still, the Skeptic's case was strong. XLP was the best sector on every horizon and Staples was the Analyst's first favored sector, so the clause fired on its letter, not its intent. The PM never addressed the Skeptic's partial-trim alternative, which a resize allowed. The design flaw came on 11-20, when 'while SPY holds' was removed and left an absolute-return threshold that any broad selloff trips. (2) The IDXX half trim (P2, filled $691.01) delivered the L8 trim that was owed, and the high-beta reasoning was sound. The PM's reply to the Skeptic's idle-cash point ('only caps the downside on half') was thin, since the proceeds cannot be redeployed while the regime filter is on. (3) The TLT resize from $20 to $10 (filled $81.11) engaged directly with the Skeptic's data objection (market.json dated 11-20, TLT 21d +0.06%). It kept TLT under the $40 rejected on 11-20 and stayed within the Skeptic's own $5-10 range. That was the best-argued call of the day. The thesis_updates fixed every L6 stale-text item the Fundamentals review had flagged (DPZ, VRSN, CARG, IDXX, KR) and restated TLT's stop from the $80.75 fill. At the close no stop is near or tripped: SAM is closest at 5.02% above $201, then INCY 6.68%, TLT 7.06% and IDXX 7.35%, with no stop_alerts. The low-beta book lagged the bounce as designed: KR -1.9% on the day, TLT +0.15%, the rest +1.2% to +2.8%. Cash is now about 52% of equity. The regime filter idles that cash, but two of today's trades added about $74 to it.
lessons: Write a sector-condition clause as a relative test when it is first stored: for example 'XLP's 21-day return falls below SPY's', or 'XLP closes below its 200-day'. Do not store a bare absolute threshold. WMT's '+3% XLP 21d' line, stripped of its SPY qualifier on 11-20, tripped on a market-wide drop while XLP was still the strongest sector. Honouring it today was correct. The fix belongs at write time, not on the day a clause trips. When a clause trips against its evident intent, say whether a resize (a partial sale) was considered and why it was rejected.

While the regime filter blocks redeployment, treat each discretionary sale as a move into idle cash for an unknown number of weeks, and weigh that cost explicitly against the risk it removes. Today's bounce left SPY roughly 1% under its 200-day (an estimate from the 4.7% rise in spy_value against the 730.28 line). The filter could reopen within a session or two. The Proposer and PM should have a ranked re-entry list ready, sized against buckets (Utilities and non-stacked names first; WMT is not wash-sale blocked after a gain sale), so deployment happens in the first run the filter allows.

L6 follow-up for the next run: restate TLT's $76.30 stop from the blended cost after the 11-23 add (about $80.85 from the $80.75 and $81.11 lots, so $76.30 is about 5.6% under it), with the text and stop_price agreeing. The stored text itself says this is due.
